observation: The released agent-loop 0.16.3 router/status surface contradicted the executable release in three places: the router expected Activation/Next status sections that were absent, it documented sync-instructions although that command/asset was not shipped, and workflow status reported ready_to_close even with failed validation evidence that workflow close correctly refused.

evidence.summary: agent-loop 0.16.3 init status printed source paths, aliases, manifests and stale entries but not the Activation/Next sections its router told agents to consume.
The 0.16.3 router described init sync-instructions and a package-managed instruction block, but the released command and source asset were absent.

workflow status reported Overall: ready_to_close and suggested workflow close while a failed observation for the declared phpunit validation command was recorded; workflow close then refused on that same evidence.

hypothesis: Release-facing instructions and the status projection were not derived from the same executable command/gate authorities used by the installed release and workflow close.
validated_conclusion: The consumer run demonstrated release/status drift in agent-loop 0.16.3: an agent following published/router output could be directed toward nonexistent commands or a close operation that the authoritative gate would reject.
